description: Fig. 15 is a composite of eight microscopic digital image correlation (μ-DIC) shear-strain field maps arranged in two rows. Row (a) is "Representative region 1" and row (b) is "Representative region 2" of the RD sample; each row contains four maps at applied strain levels 5%, 10%, 15% and 20% (printed top-left of each map). A single right-hand colour bar is labelled "Shear Strain (%)" and spans 0 to 30 in increments of 5, running from dark blue (low) through green/yellow to red (high). In every map a dashed black line marks the phase boundary separating the upper δ region (labelled "δ", δ-ferrite) from the lower γ+α aggregate region (labelled "γ+α"), a 4 µm scale bar sits bottom-left, and red arrows mark localised strain-concentration features. At 5% the fields are mostly dark blue (near-zero shear strain); with increasing applied strain the maps become progressively heterogeneous, and by 15-20% yellow-to-red high-shear-strain bands concentrate along and immediately adjacent to the dashed phase boundary in both regions. The figure demonstrates that strain localises preferentially at the δ-ferrite / UFG γ+α phase boundary, supporting the strain-incompatibility argument in the text. No numeric values are printed on the maps themselves.

observations.observation: The figure contains eight μ-DIC shear-strain maps arranged in two rows, (a) and (b), each row holding four maps labelled 5%, 10%, 15% and 20%.
A single colour bar at the right of the figure is labelled "Shear Strain (%)" and ranges from 0 to 30 in increments of 5.
Every map contains a dashed black line marking the phase boundary, with the region labelled "δ" above the line and the region labelled "γ+α" below it.
A scale bar of 4 µm is printed in the bottom-left corner of each of the eight maps.
Red arrows mark localised strain features in each map and are positioned at or close to the dashed phase boundary.
At 5% applied strain both regions appear predominantly dark blue, i.e. low shear strain across the field.
At 20% applied strain, yellow-to-red (high shear strain) bands decorate and flank the dashed phase boundary in both (a) and (b).
The spatial heterogeneity of shear strain increases monotonically with the applied strain level from 5% to 20% in both representative regions.

The caption identifies (a) as Representative region 1 and (b) as Representative region 2, showing local strain distribution close to the phase boundary of δ-ferrite and UFG γ+α aggregates of the RD sample.

The citing text states that strain concentrations are present at the phase boundary between the δ-ferrite phase and the UFG α-γ aggregate region, analogous to composite materials, and that this is supported by the μ-DIC data of Fig. 15.

The citing text states that for the RD sample the δ-ferrite phase and UFG α-γ aggregates deform to the same level to comply with an iso-strain condition, requiring a high density of GNDs to accommodate the hardness/stiffness difference.
Panel labels "(a)" and "(b)" are printed at the top-left of the two rows.

subfigures.description: Row of four μ-DIC shear-strain maps for Representative region 1 of the RD sample, at 5%, 10%, 15% and 20% applied strain. Each map has a dashed black line marking the δ-ferrite / γ+α phase boundary (δ above, γ+α below), two red arrows pointing to strain-concentration sites near the boundary, and a 4 µm scale bar. At 5% the field is mostly dark blue; by 15-20% yellow-red high-shear-strain bands flank the phase boundary.

Row of four μ-DIC shear-strain maps for Representative region 2 of the RD sample, at 5%, 10%, 15% and 20% applied strain, with the same dashed phase boundary, δ/γ+α labels, red arrows and 4 µm scale bar. The same progression from an almost uniform low-strain (blue) field at 5% to strongly localised high-shear-strain (yellow-red) bands at the phase boundary at 20% is visible.
